question: In which State will north India's first nuclear project be set up?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• North India's first nuclear power project is set to be established in the state of **Haryana**, specifically in Gorakhpur village, Fatehabad district.
 
• The project, known as the **Gorakhpur Haryana Anu Vidyut Pariyojana (GHAVP)**, is being developed by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), a public sector enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy.
 
• GHAVP will consist of two reactors, each with a capacity of **700 MW (megawatts)**, based on indigenous Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) technology.
 
• The project aims to enhance India's nuclear energy capacity and contribute significantly to meeting the country's growing energy demands.
 
• Once operational, GHAVP will provide clean and reliable energy, reducing dependency on fossil fuels and contributing to India's climate change mitigation goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uttarakhand**

 
 
• Uttarakhand is known for its **hydroelectric **power projects due to its abundant water resources and hilly terrain.
 
• Prominent hydroelectric projects include the Tehri Dam, one of India's largest hydroelectric projects, generating over 1,000 MW of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**
 
 
• Punjab primarily relies on **thermal** power plants and renewable energy sources like solar power for its electricity needs.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is a hub for **hydroelectric **power generation, with projects like the Nathpa Jhakri Hydroelectric Station contributing significantly to India's energy sector.
 
• Due to its geographic and seismic conditions, the state has not been chosen for nuclear power project development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nuclear Energy in India**

 
 
• India is one of the few countries actively expanding its nuclear energy capacity to meet growing power demands while reducing carbon emissions.
 
• Currently, India has several operational nuclear power plants, including Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu, Tarapur in Maharashtra, and Kakrapar in Gujarat.
 
• Nuclear energy contributes approximately 3% to India's total electricity generation and is expected to grow with projects like GHAVP in Haryana.
 
• The government has emphasized the development of indigenous nuclear reactor technology, such as PHWRs, to ensure self-reliance in nuclear energy.
